# Google (11 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /search | `query` | 1 | Google web search |
| /ad | `url` | 5 | Get Google ad details |
| /adlibrary/advertisers/search | `query` | 5 | Search Google Ad Library advertisers |
| /company/ads | `domain` / `advertiser_id` | 5 | List Google ads by company |
| /business/info | `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` | 1 | Get a Google Business Profile |
| /business/extended-reviews | `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` | **5-9** | Get Google extended (multi-source) reviews |
| /business/updates | `keyword` / `cid` | 1 | Get Google Business Profile posts (updates) |
| /business/questions | `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` | 5 | Get Google Business Profile questions & answers |
| /hotels/search | `keyword` | 1 | Search Google hotels |
| /hotels/info | `hotel_identifier` | 5 | Get Google hotel detail |
| /keyword-volume | `keywords` | 16 | Get Google keyword search volume by country |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /search — 1cr

Returns Google search results for a query. Each result includes title, URL, and a text snippet.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword or phrase
- `region` *(optional)*: 2 letter country code, ie US, UK, CA, etc This will show results from that country
- `date_posted` *(optional)*: Date posted
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number to retrieve Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead: the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim: the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /ad — 5cr

Returns detailed information about a specific Google advertisement including ad copy, advertiser, and format.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Ads Transparency Center CREATIVE URL: must include both the advertiser and creative segments (`…/advertiser/{AR…}/creative/{CR…}`). Get one from `/v1/google/company/ads`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/ad?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adlibrary/advertisers/search — 5cr

Searches the Google Ads Transparency Center for advertisers matching a query. Returns matching advertisers with `name`, `advertiser_id`, and `region`, plus their website domains. Defaults to US when `region` is omitted: pass a 2-letter country code (e.g. `AU`, `CA`) to search advertisers in another region.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search keyword or phrase to find advertisers in the Google Ads Transparency Center.
- `region` *(optional)*: 2-letter country code to search in. Defaults to US.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/adlibrary/advertisers/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /company/ads — 5cr

Returns ads from a specific company/domain in the Google Ads Transparency Center. Each ad includes creative, format, and date range.

> 💸 **`get_ad_details=true` changes the price to 25 credits** (base 5). openapi get_ad_details param: 'Set to true to get the ad details. Will cost 25 credits.' Base is 5. NOT measured — the 08.23.26 sweep billed the 5cr base only. Recorded in findings.md:885 as a conditional-price instance.

**Parameters**

- `topic` *(optional)*: The topic to search for. If you search for 'political', you will also need to pass a 'region', like 'US' or 'AU'
- `region` *(optional)*: The region to search for. Defaults to anywhere
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Start date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `end_date` *(optional)*: End date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `platform` *(optional)*: Google surface to filter ads by (e.g. youtube, google_search)
- `format` *(optional)*: Ad format to filter by: text, image, or video
- `get_ad_details` *(optional)*: Set to true to get the ad details. Will cost 25 credits.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Cursor to paginate through results
- `domain` / `advertiser_id` — at least one required.
  - `domain`: Company domain name to look up ads for (one of: domain, advertiser_id; at least one required)
  - `advertiser_id`: The advertiser id of the company (one of: domain, advertiser_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/company/ads?domain=<domain>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /business/info — 1cr

Returns the full Google Business Profile (Maps / Knowledge Panel) for a local business: name, category, rating, address, phone, coordinates, hours, attributes, and claimed status. Identify the place by keyword, cid, or place_id (cid/place_id are most reliable).

**Parameters**

- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country' (default 'New York,New York,United States').
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').
- `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` — at least one required.
  - `keyword`: Business name + address (e.g. 'Irving Farm New York 645 5th Ave'). Use cid/place_id when known for an exact match. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `cid`: Google customer id (cid) of the place: the most reliable identifier. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `place_id`: Google place_id of the place. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/info?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /business/extended-reviews — 5-9cr

Returns reviews of a place aggregated from the Google reviews element, not only Google users but reputable third-party sources (TripAdvisor, Yelp, Trustpilot). Each review carries its source domain, full text (with original-language translation), star rating, reviewer stats, and owner replies. Identify the place by keyword, cid, or place_id.

> ⚠️ **Metered: 5-9 credits a call — budget the 9 ceiling, not the low end.** Vendor label: 5-9 (metered): 5 credits per page. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.

**Parameters**

- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of reviews to return (default 20, step 20, max 1000).
- `label` *(optional)*: Optional CSV of SocialCrawl labels to add to every review. Without this param every page already carries sentiment and issue, free; label= adds the labels you name to them (the defaults keep running). sentiment and issue are free when asked for too; reports, incentivized and injection add 1 credit per started 25 newly judged reviews. judgments=off (or label=none) turns the default labels off. They read the review's title and text, never its stars. sentiment: how the reviewer feels, on five levels (level 0 to 4, score_0_1, confidence), plus rating_mismatch, true when the words clearly contradict the star rating (a glowing text under 1 star, a furious one under 5), null when the review has no rating. issue: the main problem the review reports (label: product_defect, sizing_or_fit, shipping_or_delivery, customer_service, price_or_value, missing_feature, other, or none, with confidence; label is null when unsure). reports (needs reports=): does this review say that the thing you describe happened (p, 0 to 1). incentivized: does the reviewer say they got the product free, discounted or rewarded for the review (p), and did the text carry a disclosure such as 'in exchange for my honest review', Vine or 체험단 (disclosed). injection flags text that addresses an AI system and tries to direct it (flagged, p); it never drops or rewrites a row. These are signals to read, never a verdict on a review or a reviewer. A review that could not be judged carries labels: null. Reviews already labelled for anyone are free, and so is a cached page. data.labels reports what was judged and billed.
- `reports` *(optional)*: Required by label=reports, ignored otherwise. What to look for, in plain words, up to 300 characters, for example reports=the battery drains quickly or reports=배송이 늦음. Every review gains labels.reports.p, the probability that it says so, in any wording or language. Without it label=reports is skipped with the warning label_reports_needs_reports and is not billed.
- `judgments` *(optional)*: Optional, on (the default) or off. By default every row gains free SocialCrawl judgments (computed.labels, and computed.relevance on search endpoints), reported in data.labels (mode default) and data.relevance (origin default), each with a status (complete, partial or skipped) and pending: the rows still being judged when the page was sent, which carry null now and are filled on your next call or cached read. Default judgments never add credits, never change an existing field, and never drop or reorder a row. off returns the page exactly as before, with none of those keys. label=none does the same.
- `dry_run` *(optional)*: Optional. When 1, return a cost preview for this labelled or relevance-filtered request without fetching the page or judging any row. data.estimate reports rows_expected, rows_cached, label_credits_min, label_credits_max and base_credits. 0 credits charged.
- `label_evidence` *(optional)*: Optional, only with label=. When 1, every labelled row also carries computed.labels_evidence.<preset> = { quote, sentence_index }: the sentence in the row that most clearly shows the label, copied verbatim. Absent or null when no single sentence shows it.
- `fit` *(optional)*: Optional. When goal, keep the rows and fields needed for the goal you pass in goal= (plus any that are uncertain, and the first and last), and replace the rest with a stub. data.held_back lists the held ids and a recall id that re-reads the full page from cache at no extra charge. Without this param the page is unchanged.
- `goal` *(optional)*: Required by fit=goal. What you are trying to do, in your own words, up to 300 characters.
- `fit_tokens` *(optional)*: Optional, only with fit=goal. Soft cap on how much of the page to keep, in tokens. Uncertain blocks and the first and last block are kept even if they exceed it.
- `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` — at least one required.
  - `keyword`: Business name + address. Use cid/place_id for an exact match. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `cid`: Google customer id (cid) of the place. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `place_id`: Google place_id of the place. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/extended-reviews?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /business/updates — 1cr

Returns the owner-published posts (updates) on a Google Business Profile: text, image, publish date, and any call-to-action link. Most businesses publish none; an empty result is a valid 'no posts' answer. Identify the business by keyword or cid.

**Parameters**

- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').
- `keyword` / `cid` — at least one required.
  - `keyword`: Business name + location (e.g. 'Toyota of Manhattan New York'). (one of: keyword, cid; at least one required)
  - `cid`: Google customer id (cid) of the business. (one of: keyword, cid; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/updates?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /business/questions — 5cr

Returns the community Q&A on a Google Business Profile: each question and its answers flattened into one comment list linked by parent_id. Identify the business by keyword, cid, or place_id.

**Parameters**

- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').
- `depth` *(optional)*: Number of questions to return (default 20).
- `keyword` / `cid` / `place_id` — at least one required.
  - `keyword`: Business name + location (e.g. 'Starbucks Reserve Roastery New York'). (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `cid`: Google customer id (cid) of the business. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)
  - `place_id`: Google place_id of the business. (one of: keyword, cid, place_id; at least one required)

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/questions?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /hotels/search — 1cr

Returns hotels for a query from Google Travel: name, star rating, review score, coordinates, images, and nightly price. Dates default to next-day / one-night / two-visitors when omitted. Each hotel_identifier can be passed to GET /v1/google/hotels/info for full detail.

**Parameters**

- `keyword`: Hotel search query (e.g. 'hotels in New York').
- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').
- `check_in` *(optional)*: Check-in date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the next day.
- `check_out` *(optional)*: Check-out date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to one night.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/hotels/search?keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /hotels/info — 5cr

Returns full detail for a hotel by its hotel_identifier (from GET /v1/google/hotels/search): description, star rating, address, phone, coordinates, amenities across 14 categories, 27 review-sentiment topics, and a multi-vendor price comparison.

**Parameters**

- `hotel_identifier`: Opaque hotel id returned by GET /v1/google/hotels/search.
- `location_name` *(optional)*: Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` *(optional)*: Result language (default 'English').

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/hotels/info?hotel_identifier=<hotel_identifier>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /keyword-volume — 16cr

Returns Google monthly search volume, cost per click, competition, and a 12-month trend for up to 20 keywords in one country. Response is `{ location, location_name, language, items }`: each item carries `keyword`, `search_volume` (average monthly searches), `cpc` with its `currency`, `competition` (0 to 1) with `competition_level`, `monthly_searches` (the last 12 months, oldest first, as `{ year, month, search_volume }`) and, where Google classifies it, `search_intent`. Use it to compare demand for a product across markets: call it once per country with the same keywords. You get one item per keyword you asked for, in your order. A keyword Google holds no volume for comes back with `search_volume: null`, never 0, so a null means unknown and a 0 means Google reports none. When no keyword has any data the call returns 404 and costs 0 credits. Volumes are Google's own rounded monthly averages and are refreshed monthly, so results are cached for 24 hours. Typical latency is 2 seconds. Priced at a flat 16 credits per call whatever the keyword count, so send all 20 at once.

**Parameters**

- `keywords`: 1-20 comma-separated keywords (e.g. 'lip gloss,lip oil'). Each keyword may be up to 80 characters. Duplicates are ignored. More than 20 keywords, or a keyword over 80 characters, is rejected with a free 400 before the request is billed.
- `location` *(optional)*: Country as an ISO code ('US', 'GB', 'KR'), a full country name ('United Kingdom', 'South Korea') or a numeric location code ('2826'). Defaults to the United States. Volume is published for 94 countries; any other location is rejected with a free 400 naming the accepted forms.
- `language` *(optional)*: Language code ('en', 'de', 'ko') the keywords are searched in. Defaults to the first language listed for the country: Germany is 'de' and Belgium is 'fr', but Vietnam, Indonesia, India, Malaysia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Hong Kong and Singapore default to 'en', so pass their local language (e.g. 'vi', 'id', 'hi') explicitly. A language the country does not hold (Germany in English) is rejected with a free 400 listing the ones it does.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/keyword-volume?keywords=<keywords>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Google endpoint

Three unrelated jobs live under this platform: web search, the Google Ads transparency
library, and Google Business Profiles (the local/maps listing). Pick by job, not by name.

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| A plain web search | `/search` | 1 |
| What ads is this company running on Google? | `/company/ads` | 5 |
| Find the advertiser record first | `/adlibrary/advertisers/search` | 5 |
| One ad's creative and metadata | `/ad` | 5 |
| A local business's listing | `/business/info` | 1 |
| What that business posts | `/business/updates` | 1 |
| Q&A on the listing | `/business/questions` | 5 |
| Reviews, pulled from several sources | `/business/extended-reviews` | 5 |
| Hotels | `/hotels/search` (1) then `/hotels/info` (5) | 1 / 5 |

### The ad library is a two-step

You usually cannot go straight to `/company/ads` — resolve the advertiser first with
`/adlibrary/advertisers/search` (5cr), then pull their ads (5cr). Budget 10cr for "what ads is
X running on Google", and compare against Facebook's ad library (`facebook/adlibrary/*`, also
5cr), which is the richer source for most consumer brands.

### Business Profile: check the cheap ones first

`/business/info` and `/business/updates` are 1cr; `/business/questions` and
`/business/extended-reviews` are 5cr. If you only need star rating, category, hours or
location, `/business/info` alone answers it. `extended-reviews` is worth 5cr only when you
want review *text* from multiple sources — for a reputation verdict across Trustpilot and the
app stores as well, `prism/reputation` (30cr) is the one-call version.

### `/search` is a 1cr rung on the search ladder

When the platform is "the open web", `google/search` (1cr) is the cheapest answer — far below
`search/everywhere` (20cr). See the search ladder in the skill body.
